subject: Pharos AI — MAP: capacity onramp & activation cadence
messages:

Cc: Ethan Cho <ethan@pharos.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kick-off: capacity needs & lead times

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Pharos is excited about the latency profile and the private deployment options. We want to start a short MAP that covers evaluation milestones and an initial capacity reservation to cover our Q3 pilot. High-level asks from our side:

- Understand Redwood Dedicated + Private lead times for H100 / A100 pools (we have a preference for H100 where possible).
- A recommended GPU pool sizing for a 3-month pilot (~100M tokens/day peak, batchy workloads).
- An evaluation plan cadence we can run with our infra team (SLOs: 95th latency < 150ms, 99th < 400ms for generation).

Can you propose an activation cadence and what the procurement handoff timeline looks like (we have an internal procurement cycle that needs a 3-week lead for POs)? Happy to loop procurement on follow-ups.

Best,
Sophie Lane
Head of ML Platforms, Pharos AI
[sophie@pharos.ai]

Subject: Re: MAP kick-off: capacity needs & lead times

Sophie — appreciate the clear asks. I put together a short starter MAP focused on getting you from evaluation to commitment with concrete milestones and decision gates. Summary below; I'll attach a living spreadsheet with timelines.

Quick proposal (starter MAP):
- Week 0–2: Eval kickoff — access to private sandbox, baseline perf tests, integration checklist.
- Week 3–4: Ramp tests — workload replay, batching experiments, KV cache tuning.
- Week 5–6: Pilot readiness — SLA run, cost projection, security/ SOC2 evidence.
- Week 7–8: Procurement & reservation — sign PO, reserve tranche, onboarding schedule.

GPU sizing suggestion (initial reserve):
- Pilot baseline: 8 H100 GPUs (1–2 nodes) for bursty peak; 4 H100 for steady state.
- Contingency tranche: +4 H100 available within 6–8 weeks (dedicated pool).

I asked Ben to validate the sizing and timeline against similar pilots; Lauren will coordinate the SOC2/evidence for your auditors.

Attached: starter_map_v1.xlsx (I'll update after internal sizing review).

Cheers,
Monica Patel

Looping in sizing notes (from similar mid-market pilots).

Monica / Sophie — a few practical sizing recommendations based on the 100M tokens/day peak you mentioned:
- Estimate token mix (gen vs embed vs rerank). If >80% gen with long contexts, compute needs grow non-linear. For conservative planning assume 1.8x compute vs short-chat baseline.
- For a 3-month pilot, start with 6–8 H100 for active serving and a warm-standby of 2 H100 for fast failovers. If you can accept a slightly higher 95th latency during non-business hours, you can stagger capacity (i.e., turn up to 10 H100 only for scheduled peak windows).
- Lead times: Dedicated H100 pool reservation: typical procurement + allocation -> 5–7 weeks. Private/on-prem appliance deliveries vary by vendor but budget 8–12 weeks for hardware + network setup.

I'll model a two-tranche reservation in the spreadsheet: immediate pilot tranche + optional fast-activation tranche.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
To: monica_patel@redwood-inference.com, ben_carter@redwood-inference.com, Sophie Lane <sophie@pharos.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation plan: tests, gates, and acceptance criteria

Hi all — some specifics to make the MAP actionable from an eval perspective. I recommend we codify the following checkpoints and artifacts:

1) Performance baseline (Day 0–7)
- Artifact: perf-report-day0.json, first-pass latency heatmap, token-cost baseline.
- Gate: 95th percentile P50 baseline within 120–180ms (depends on context size).

2) Stress & scaling tests (Week 2–4)
- Artifact: load-run-logs.tar.gz, autoscale policy config, batch-size matrix.
- Gate: graceful degradation with 10% throughput drop before falling back to lower-cost model variants.

3) Security/compliance (Week 3–5)
- Artifact: SOC2 evidence bundle, VPC peering checklist.
- Gate: security sign-off from Pharos engineering and evidence received by procurement.

4) Cost & forecast (Week 4–6)
- Artifact: cost-forecast.xlsx with amortized GPU-hour and token-cost.
- Gate: procurement-approved budget for tranche 1.

5) Procurement handoff (Week 6–8)
- Artifact: PO template + mutual acceptance email thread.
- Gate: signed PO and reserved tranche in Redwood Dedicated.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the perf tests and share thresholds we recommend for your SLOs.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime Optimization

Subject: Pharos MAP v2 (timeline + activation cadence)

Sophie / Ethan — attached is MAP v2 with concrete dates and a two-tranche reservation plan that aligns with your 3-week procurement cycle. Highlights:

- Tranche A (pilot): 6 H100 active + 2 H100 warm standby — target reserved by 2027-06-21 to enable a July pilot start.
- Tranche B (scale): +6 H100 on call, activation window 6 weeks after PO; target reserve decision by 2027-07-12.
- Evaluation milestones map to Karthik's checkpoints; we've assigned owners and delivery dates in the sheet.
- Procurement notes: we can accept a PO and place a soft reservation while SOC2 evidence bundle is assembled. Final capacity allocation completes once PO is live.

Next steps / asks:
1) Sophie / Procurement: confirm PO lead time (you previously noted 3 weeks). Can procurement share a target PO date?
2) Ethan / Infra: confirm whether Pharos prefers hard isolation (private VPC) vs dedicated pooled tenancy (for faster activation). This affects provisioning lead time.
3) Internal (Ben/Karthik): finalize the sizing model by EOD Friday so I can push MAP v3.

Attachments included: pharos_map_v3.xlsx, h100_pool_sizing_v2.pdf, SOC2-evidence-request.docx

Thanks — ready to move to procurement handoff once you confirm dates.

—Monica
